UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user interacting with the LetterBoard application. This entity stores basic profile information and references an external authentication system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity, typically linked to an external authentication system's user ID.

username.description: A display name chosen by the user.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

Room.title: Room
Room.description: Represents a shared messaging board where users can exchange messages. Rooms are identified by a unique 4-letter code.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Room entity.

code.description: A unique 4-letter code used for joining the room.

name.description: An optional descriptive name for the room, set by the creator.

creatorId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who created this room. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Room)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the room was created.

Message.title: Message
Message.description: Represents a single text message sent within a room, displayed as a movable element on the board.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Message entity.

roomId.description: Reference to the Room where this message was sent. (Relationship: Room 1:N Message)

senderId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who sent this message. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Message)

content.description: The actual text content of the message.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the message was sent.

positionX.description: The X-coordinate of the message on the board, allowing for drag-and-drop functionality.

positionY.description: The Y-coordinate of the message on the board, allowing for drag-and-drop functionality.

classification.description: An optional classification of the message's relation to other content on the board (e.g., 'adds information', 'contradicts'), generated by the GenAI tool.

definition.description: Stores individual user profile information. The document ID `{userId}` corresponds to the authenticated user's ID (`request.auth.uid`), ensuring path-based ownership. Access is strictly limited to the owning user for read/write operations.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, matching their Firebase Authentication UID.

definition.description: Represents a collaborative messaging board. Each document contains a `creatorId` and a `members` map (e.g., `members: { 'uid1': true, 'uid2': true }`) to define who has access. Authorization for the room document itself relies on `request.auth.uid` matching `creatorId` for creator-specific actions or being present in the `members` map for general member access.

params.name: roomId
params.description: The unique identifier for the room.

definition.description: Contains individual messages within a specific room. To ensure authorization independence, each message document includes denormalized fields from its parent room: `roomCreatorId` (a copy of `Room.creatorId`) and `roomMembers` (a copy of the `Room.members` map). This allows security rules to authorize access based solely on the message document's data, without `get()` calls to the parent room.

params.name: roomId
params.description: The unique identifier of the parent room to which this message belongs.

params.name: messageId
params.description: The unique identifier for the message within the room.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure prioritizes Authorization Independence and Query-Aware Security (QAP) principles. 

1.  **User Profiles (`/userProfiles/{userId}`):** User profiles are stored in a top-level collection, with the document ID matching the authenticated user's UID (`request.auth.uid`). This establishes clear path-based ownership, making authorization trivial: a user can only read/write their own profile. This inherently supports Authorization Independence as no `get()` calls to other documents are needed, and QAPs are simple as queries on this path for a specific `userId` are naturally filtered by the path itself.

2.  **Rooms (`/rooms/{roomId}`):** Rooms are stored in a top-level collection. Each `Room` document includes a `creatorId` (referencing the `UserProfile` who created it) and a `members` map. The `members` map (`members: { [uid: string]: boolean }`) explicitly lists all users authorized to access the room, adhering to the 'Membership Map' strategy for collaborative data. Authorization for a `Room` document relies solely on `request.auth.uid` matching `creatorId` or being present in the `members` map, ensuring Authorization Independence for the `Room` document itself. QAPs are supported by allowing `list` operations filtered by the `members` map (e.g., `where('members.' + request.auth.uid, '==', true)`).

3.  **Messages (`/rooms/{roomId}/messages/{messageId}`):** Messages are stored in a subcollection nested under their respective `Room` documents. To strictly adhere to the 'Authorization Independence' mandate (avoiding `get()` calls to parent documents in rules) and enable secure `list` operations (QAPs), each `Message` document **MUST denormalize** critical authorization context from its parent `Room`. Specifically, each `Message` document will include `roomCreatorId` (a copy of `Room.creatorId`) and `roomMembers` (a copy of the entire `Room.members` map). This denormalization ensures that security rules for `Message` documents can evaluate authorization (read/write access) by inspecting `request.resource.data.roomMembers[request.auth.uid]` directly within the message document, without needing to perform a `get()` on the parent `Room`. While this introduces a fan-out write challenge when `Room.members` changes (requiring an update to all child `Message` documents), it strictly meets the requirement for Authorization Independence and simplifies robust security rules for list queries on messages within a room.
